summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease and newly diagnosed high-grade osteosarcoma of the left tibia was admitted for her first cycle of adjuvant chemotherapy with doxorubicin and cisplatin. She had recently undergone tumor resection and was recovering at home with ongoing narcotic pain management. A port was successfully placed on admission for chemotherapy access. She tolerated the treatment well, with only transient mild chest pressure that resolved spontaneously and normal cardiac workup. Her anemia, related to chronic hemolysis from sickle cell disease, was managed with a single unit of packed red blood cells prior to discharge. She remained stable throughout the hospitalization, received pegfilgrastim (Neulasta) to support white blood cell recovery, and was discharged home with clear instructions on infection prevention, medication management, and follow-up for subsequent chemotherapy cycles.
